title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview
=======
This document centralizes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for areas that apply across teams: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended to be a single reference for employees, managers, and approvers.

Scope and ownership
-------------------
- Owner: people-ops (primary), with functional owners: security, finance-legal, eng-sre, procurement.
- Audience: all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors.
- Status: Published. Updates should follow the Change Management section below.

1) Access & permissions (RBAC and onboarding/offboarding)
-----------------------------------------------------
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, consistent onboarding/offboarding, and auditable access grants.

Key roles and definitions:
- RBAC roles: viewer, developer, maintainer, admin, super-admin.
- Resource domains: code (GitHub), infra (cloud accounts), data (S3 buckets, internal datastores), product (project boards, analytics).

Standard procedures:
1. New hires/contractors:
   - People-ops creates the onboarding ticket in the HR tracker and tags the relevant team lead and security.
   - Minimum baseline access for new hires: viewer access to docs, HR systems, Slack, and identity account. Additional access requires team lead request via Access Request form.
   - Access Requests must include: justification, requested role, resources, and expiration (if temporary).
2. Temporary access:
   - All temporary accesses require an explicit expiration date and automatic revocation. Max renewal period is 90 days.
3. Offboarding:
   - People-ops triggers the offboarding workflow on termination/resignation. Security and IT must confirm revocation of cloud keys, GitHub access, and device enrollment within 24 hours of offboarding completion.

Approval and audit:
- All production-level access to infra and data must be approved by the resource owner and security.
- Quarterly access review: Team leads receive an access report and must confirm or revoke accesses. Security runs an automated reconciliation and reports exceptions monthly.

Secrets and key management:
- Secrets must be stored in our corporate KMS or approved vault (e.g., KMS/HSM integrations). Hard-coded secrets in repositories are prohibited.
- API keys for third-party services must be stored in the secrets manager and rotated per vendor SLA or at least annually.

2) Change management (infrastructure and service changes)
-------------------------------------------------------
Purpose: Reduce incidents caused by poorly planned changes and enable predictable coordination for cross-team work. Applies to infra, core services, and public APIs.

Change categories:
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-authorized (routine config updates, minor infra scaling). Requires change ticket and notification to affected teams.
- Minor change: moderate risk (non-breaking schema changes, non-customer-facing deploys). Requires peer review and SRE/owner sign-off.
- Major change: high risk (database migrations, production schema changes, network changes). Requires formal Change Request (CR), rollback plan, test runbook, scheduled maintenance window, and pre-approval from Eng Platform and SRE.

Change request workflow:
1. Create CR in Change Tracker with: description, owner, risk classification, rollback plan, test checklist, communication plan, and impacted services.
2. Peer review and automated CI checks.
3. SRE/Eng Platform review: validate rollback plan and monitoring hooks.
4. Schedule and announce maintenance window (48 hours notice recommended for major changes).
5. Execute change with runbook, monitor metrics, and escalate if abnormal.
6. Post-change review: update the CR with status, metrics, and lessons learned.

SLOs and guardrails:
- Emergency changes must be documented within 24 hours of execution.
- For major changes, define clear SLO rollback thresholds (e.g., 5xx spike > 0.5% above baseline sustained for 5 minutes triggers rollback).

3) Data management (classification, retention, access, backups)
-------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose: Protect customer and company data while enabling safe analytics and development.

Data classification:
- Public: information intended for public consumption.
- Internal: company-internal information with no regulatory constraints.
- Restricted: PII, customer data, model inputs/outputs tied to customers, and regulated data.

Policies by classification:
- Restricted data:
  - Must be stored in approved encrypted storage with access logged.
  - Data retention is defined per dataset and approved by Data Governance (typical retention 1\u20137 years depending on regulation).
  - Masking and anonymization are required for analytics pipelines unless explicit approval is documented.
- Internal data: accessible on a least-privilege basis.

Backups and disaster recovery:
- Critical production data snapshots: daily incremental, weekly full backups; test recovery quarterly.
- Backup encryption at rest and in transit required.

Data lifecycle and deletion:
- Data owners must document retention requirements and deletion procedures in the Data Inventory.
- Deletion requests (legal/custodial) must be routed to Data Governance and executed within SLA (30 days standard, 7 days for urgent/legal).

Logging and monitoring:
- Access to restricted datasets must be logged and reviewed monthly. Suspicious access is escalated to security.

4) Procurement and expenses (requests, approvals, corporate cards)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose: Maintain control and visibility over company spend while enabling teams to operate efficiently.

Procurement channels:
- Small purchases (< $5,000): Team lead approval. Use corporate card or procurement portal.
- Medium purchases ($5,000\u2013$50,000): Require department head approval and procurement team notification. Competitive quotes (2+) recommended for hardware or multi-year SaaS commitments.
- Large purchases (> $50,000): Procurement + finance legal review and executive sign-off (VP/GM). Formal RFP recommended for complex engagements.

Expense policy:
- Employees must submit expenses within 30 days of incurring cost. Receipts required for all purchases > $25.

Vendor contracting and payment:
- All vendors must be on an approved vendor list maintained by procurement.
- Contract signature authority: legal + finance for all > $25,000 commitments.

5) Vendor management and risk assessment
--------------------------------------
Purpose: Standardize onboarding and ongoing governance for third-party vendors.

Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Vendor questionnaire filled and returned (security, data handling, SOC/ISO attestation if available).
2. Risk classification (low, medium, high) by procurement and security.
3. Contract review: include data protection addenda, security SLAs, and termination rights.
4. Technical onboarding: least-privilege integration, API keys in vault, and monitoring hooks.

Ongoing vendor governance:
- Annual security and performance review for medium/high risk vendors.
- For vendors handling restricted data, require annual SOC2/ISO or equivalent audit evidence and quarterly security attestations.
- Vendor incidents: vendor must notify Redwood within 24 hours of a security incident affecting Redwood data. Procurement and security will triage and escalate per incident response procedures.

6) Travel policy (business travel, per-diem, approvals, COVID/health considerations)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose: Enable safe and cost-effective travel with clear approval and reimbursement rules.

Pre-travel approvals:
- Domestic travel: manager approval required for trips > 1 day or > $500 estimated spend.
- International travel: department head approval required. All international travel requires travel registry entry and emergency contact information.

Booking and allowable expenses:
- Use approved travel vendors for flights and hotels when available. Economy (for flights < 6 hours), Premium Economy/Business require manager approval.
- Meals: reimbursable with receipts up to per-diem limits by city.
- Ground transportation: preferred options are rideshare or corporate car service for safety; taxis/rideshares reimbursable with receipts.

Health and safety:
- Travelers must complete any required pre-travel health checks and follow both Redwood\u2019s guidance and local government requirements.

Expense submission and timelines:
- Submit travel expenses within 14 days of trip completion using the expense system. Late submissions may be denied.

7) Internal templates and forms
------------------------------
Central templates (available in the Templates library):
- Access Request form (Access Request template link)
- Change Request (CR) template with rollback checklist
- Vendor security questionnaire template
- Procurement request and quotation comparison template
- Travel authorization form and expense report template
- Offboarding checklist

Use and versioning:
- Templates are maintained in a shared Templates library. Changes to templates must be approved by the owning team and versioned with a short changelog.

Governance, exceptions, and change control
----------------------------------------
- Exceptions: Any deviation from these policies requires an Exception Request submitted to security or finance-legal depending on the domain, with an expiration and compensating controls.
- Policy updates: Major policy changes require an in_review period of at least two weeks and notification to all employees. Minor clarifications can be published by the owning team with a 72-hour notice.
- Enforcement: Policy compliance is enforced by people-ops, security, procurement, and finance. Non-compliance may lead to revocation of access, procurement holds, or disciplinary action depending on severity.
